method: First reasoned review: atomscan slow-mode JSON and cleave facts on every original, rizin control-flow disassembly, direct PE/resource/header reads, and independent Authenticode image hashing. No sample code executed. Scanner scores, collector labels and previous reviews did not establish behavior.
identification: Three damaged, memory-layout StormAttack resource-DLL installer/injector variants, with identical .text and .data. The collector names WannaCry, Remcos and Elex do not establish those families.
execution_paths: CRT entry 0x402674 calls dispatcher 0x401cb0. All three have dword 3 at 0x404120, selecting Active Setup installation and self-deletion. Alternate modes 1, 2 and 4 preserve service hijacking, service installation/dispatch and resource DLL injection respectively; their presence is capability evidence, not observed execution.

0x401900 calls GUID generator 0x401840; constructs a GUID-named EXE in a configured Windows directory; creates HKLM Active Setup Installed Components/<GUID>; writes the copy path as StubPath REG_EXPAND_SZ at 0x401a4b. It reads its own file through fopen/fseek/ftell/fread, patches the image, writes the clone with fwrite and launches that path with CreateProcessA at 0x401b7e.

0x401260 opens HKLM SYSTEM/CurrentControlSet/Services/LanmanServer/Parameters. RegDeleteValueA at 0x401320 removes ServiceDLL; RegSetValueExA at 0x40133e replaces the same value with a 128-byte REG_EXPAND_SZ buffer constructed from %SystemRoot%/System32/ and the payload DLL name. This is distinct from the query-only path at 0x401d35.

0x402460 loads resource type DLL/id 101, obtains its size and bytes, copies them unchanged, and calls file writer 0x4023c0. The mode-1 dispatcher links the DLL drop to core-service replacement and remote loading.

0x401150 obtains an iexplore/notepad/calc executable target via 0x4010c0, creates the process, allocates memory in it with VirtualAllocEx, writes the DLL path via WriteProcessMemory, resolves Kernel32.LoadLibraryA, and passes that export with the remote path buffer to CreateRemoteThread at 0x40123d.

0x401390 obtains its own module path and short path, reads COMSPEC, builds /c del <self> > nul, creates a detached suspended shell process, adjusts priorities and resumes the thread. The dispatcher reaches this after Active Setup installation and after other successful installation branches.

Mode 2 calls service installer 0x401fd0: copies itself to the configured Windows directory, sets the installed path attributes to 6 (HIDDEN|SYSTEM) via SetFileAttributesA at 0x402181, creates an automatic SERVICE_WIN32_OWN_PROCESS service with CreateServiceA at 0x4021de, starts it and writes its Description. Its service callback drops and injects the resource DLL.

damage_and_provenance.c211c2fee3c8: 61440-byte unsigned PE. Entire .rsrc is zero-filled, including its resource directory; a usable DLL cannot be recovered there.
damage_and_provenance.f84fe0206622: 81232-byte PE with the same erased resources. Appended 19792-byte WIN_CERTIFICATE/PKCS7 blob claims Microsoft Corporation; signed image digest does not match this file. It is not evidence of Microsoft authorship of this loader.
damage_and_provenance.83bae47286ce: 81286-byte PE. DLL/101/language 2052 points to 39936 bytes at offset 0x5060. Embedded PE base 0x10000000, entry RVA 0x741a. Its .data retains family/configuration/HTTP strings, but the entry and all bytes from resource-relative 0x1800 through 0x9c00 are zero; imports/exports refer into erased regions, and no executable section survives. The same Microsoft certificate blob is appended, followed by a 54-byte trailer; its image digest mismatches too.
damage_and_provenance.memory_layout: The outer IAT contains pre-resolved addresses and a UUID overwrites part of that region. Disk-patch offsets in the self-copy routine differ from the surviving memory-layout configuration locations. These are damaged artifacts, not demonstrated working installations.
damage_and_provenance.obfuscation: No executable decryption or decompression stage was found. The resource is copied directly. The decoded URL fact derives from a printf-style GUID format string containing percent directives; no hidden network URL or decoding routine is established by that scanner-produced representation.
damage_and_provenance.limits: No runtime success, live DDoS, ransomware encryption, credential theft, Remcos payload or actual network contact is established. The private-IP/configuration/HTTP strings in the erased DLL do not restore its missing code.
damage_and_provenance.external: All three supplied tria.ge links were inaccessible through the web reader. No external verdict or sandbox score was used as proof. No deployment authorization, execution logs or distribution provenance was supplied.

verdict_basis: MALICIOUS for all three: the linked design replaces a core service DLL, creates persistent self-copies, transfers DLL execution into unrelated processes and deletes the original; a separate branch conceals an automatically started service executable. The explicit core-service hijack and concealed reactivation tip the balance over a generic installer or debugger explanation. Damage limits functionality, not the purpose supported by surviving code. An authorized research/deployment context is unknown.

finding_review.hostile: Retained all four existing hostile findings: independent self-delete, Active Setup persistence, LanmanServer replacement, and StormAttack injector identity. Each is supported by traced code; names/descriptions correctly say code rather than observed successful installation.
finding_review.suspicious: Retained remote-DLL resolved-export handoff in all three, and both signature-digest findings in the two certificate-bearing files. Independent exclusion-based SHA256 computation also mismatched the embedded signed digest in both.
finding_review.embedded_member: Its existing 50 findings are unchanged. Notable family/configuration/HTTP references and erased-entry metadata remain accurate. No hostile active DDoS/C2/download behavior was added to missing code. The embedded member's low ML probability is consistent with its zeroed code and is not an outer-file verdict disagreement.
finding_review.addition: One notable x86 hidden/system attribute-call trait under micro-behaviors/fs/attributes/flags. It binds mask 6 or 7 and the file-path push to the SetFileAttributesA IAT slot inside an executable section. It does not infer malicious intent, a service, persistence or runtime success.
finding_review.placement: Hidden/System flag modification belongs to the existing fs/attributes/flags leaf. No new directory, rule relocation, shared-rule weakening, exclusion, severity reduction or classifier-driven duplicate was introduced.
finding_review.consumer_audit: No existing selector directly selects the new rule or the entire flags/attributes directory. Broad fs selectors in the resource-observation metadata profiles already match these samples via other filesystem traits; those findings remain unchanged. No archive or fetched dependency supplies the added behavior.

controls.positive: All three original samples; six minimal neutral PE fixtures covering masks 6/7 and EAX/ECX/EDX path arguments. Neutral fixtures produce no suspicious or hostile detections.
controls.negative: Masks 0/1/2/4/128, wrong IAT slot, API-name substitution, and the identical byte sequence in a non-executable section do not match.

comparison.marker_line: StormAttack loader: hijack/inject/persist; detect hidden-system call
StormAttack loader: hijack/persist, invalid signature; add flag call
Damaged StormAttack loader: hijack/persist/inject; add attribute call

remaining_disagreements: None for the outer verdicts or supported attack coverage. Aggregate atomscan scores/levels stay unchanged. Erased DLL bytes do not justify inferring a working payload or adopting the collector family labels.
